arxiv-1802-08437.title: Abstract Completion, Formalized
arxiv-1802-08437.creator: Nao Hirokawa \rsuper a, Aart Middeldorp \rsuper b, Christian Sternagel \rsuper b, Sarah Winkler \rsuper b
arxiv-1802-08437.description: Abstract . Completion is one of the most studied techniques in term rewriting and fundamental to automated reasoning with equalities. In this paper we present new correctness proofs of abstract completion, both for finite and infinite runs. For the special case of ground completion we present a new proof based on random descent.

arxiv-2012-08952.title: Scenario-aware and Mutual-based approach for Multi-scenario Recommendation in E-Commerce
arxiv-2012-08952.creator: Yuting Chen 1,2∗ , Yanshi Wang 2∗ , Yabo Ni 2 , An-Xiang Zeng 2 , Lanfen Lin 1
arxiv-2012-08952.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yuting Chen 1,2∗ , Yanshi Wang 2∗ , Yabo Ni 2 , An-Xiang Zeng 2 , Lanfen Lin 1. Recommender systems (RSs) are essential for e-commerce platforms to help meet the enormous needs of users. How to capture user interests and make accurate recommendations for users in heterogeneous e-commerce scenarios is still a continuous research topic. However, most existing studies overlook the intrinsic association of the scenarios: the log data collected from platforms can be naturally divided into different scenarios (e.g., country, city, culture).

arxiv-2104-11994.title: Turnaround radius in Λ \Lambda CDM , and dark matter cosmologies with shear and vorticity.
arxiv-2104-11994.creator: Antonino Del Popolo, Man Ho Chan, David F. Mota
arxiv-2104-11994.description: Abstract We determine the relationship between the turnaround radius, R t R_{\rm t} , and mass, M t M_{\rm t} , in Λ \Lambda CDM, and in dark energy scenarios, using an extended spherical collapse model taking into account the effects of shear and vorticity.

arxiv-2205-09881.title: Pre-Supernova Alert System for Super-Kamiokande
arxiv-2205-09881.creator: L. N. Machado, K. Abe, Y. Hayato, K. Hiraide, K. Ieki, M. Ikeda, J. Kameda, Y. Kanemura, R.. Kaneshima, Y. Kashiwagi, Y. Kataoka, S. Miki, S. Mine, M. Miura, S. Moriyama, Y. Nakano, M. Nakahata, S. Nakayama, Y. Noguchi, K. Okamoto, K. Sato, H. Sekiya, H. Shiba, K. Shimizu, M. Shiozawa, Y. Sonoda, Y.
arxiv-2205-09881.description: Abstract In 2020, the Super-Kamiokande (SK) experiment moved to a new stage (SK-Gd) in which gadolinium (Gd) sulfate octahydrate was added to the water in the detector, enhancing the efficiency to detect thermal neutrons and consequently improving the sensitivity to low energy electron anti-neutrinos from inverse beta decay (IBD) interactions.

arxiv-2306-01753.title: Preconditioned Visual Language Inference with Weak Supervision
arxiv-2306-01753.creator: Ehsan Qasemi, Amani R. Maina-Kilaas, Devadutta Dash, Khalid Alsaggaf, Muhao Chen † \dagger Department of Computer Science, University of Southern California
arxiv-2306-01753.description: Abstract Humans can infer the affordance of objects by extracting related contextual preconditions for each scenario. For example, upon seeing an image with a broken cup, we can infer that this precondition prevents the cup from being used for drinking. Reasoning with preconditions of commonsense is studied in NLP where the model explicitly gets the contextual precondition.

arxiv-2402-08124.title: Anisotropic molecular photoemission dynamics: Interpreting and accounting for the nuclear motion
arxiv-2402-08124.creator: Antoine Desrier, Morgan Berkane, Camille Lévêque, Richard Taïeb, Jérémie Caillat
arxiv-2402-08124.description: Abstract We investigate how vibration affects molecular photoemission dynamics, through simulations on two-dimension asymmetric model molecules including the electronic and nuclear motions in a fully correlated way. We show that a slight anisotropy in the electron-ion momentum sharing is sufficient to prevent one from unambigously characterizing the vibrationnaly averaged photoemission dynamics in terms of stereo Wigner delays.

arxiv-2404-19425.title: Pinned Ad-colloids Disfavors Nucleation in Colloidal Vapor Deposition
arxiv-2404-19425.creator: Noman Hanif Barbhuiya, Pritam K. Mohanty, Saikat Mondal, Aminul Hussain, Adhip Agarwala, Chandan K. Mishra
arxiv-2404-19425.description: Abstract Crystallization through vapor deposition is ubiquitous, and is inevitably influenced by impurities, which often impact the local structure. Interestingly, the effect of immobilizing some of the depositing particles themselves, which would still preserve local structural symmetry, remains largely unexplored. Herein, we perform colloidal vapor deposition on a substrate with a few pinned ad-colloids, termed “mobility impurities”.

arxiv-2405-14801.title: Pseudospin density wave instability in two-dimensional electron bilayers
arxiv-2405-14801.creator: Jihang Zhu, Tessa Cookmeyer, Sankar Das Sarma
arxiv-2405-14801.description: Abstract We investigate the instability of layer pseudospin paramagnetic (PSP) state to the formation of pseudospin density wave (PSDW) in two-dimensional (2D) electron bilayers, analogous to the formation of Overhauser spin density wave (SDW) in a single-layer 2D electron gas (2DEG) with spin 1/2.

arxiv-2510-12097.creator: Joshua Roberson, Matthew B. Bayliss, M.D. Gladders, Gourav Khullar, Keren Sharon, Keunho Kim, Dan Coe, Lindsey Bleem, Taweewat Somboonpanyakul
arxiv-2510-12097.description: Abstract Understanding the properties of the first generation of galaxies is an ongoing challenge in observational astrophysics. While advances in deep field observation have led to the identification of large numbers of galaxies within the Epoch of Reionization, there are very few observed galaxies at this range that are sufficiently bright for high signal-to-noise spectroscopy.

arxiv-2601-14124.title: Style Transfer as Bias Mitigation: Diffusion Models for Synthetic Mental Health Text for Arabic
arxiv-2601-14124.creator: Saad Mankarious, Ayah Zirikly
arxiv-2601-14124.description: Abstract Synthetic data offers a promising solution for mitigating data scarcity and demographic bias in mental health analysis, yet existing approaches largely rely on pretrained large language models (LLMs), which may suffer from limited output diversity and propagate biases inherited from their training data.

pmc-10529757.title: Optogenetic Activation of Astrocytes Reduces Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption via IL-10 In Stroke
pmc-10529757.creator: Qian Suo, Lidong Deng, Tingting Chen, Shengju Wu, Lin Qi, Ze Liu, Tingting He, Heng-Li Tian, Wanlu Li, Yaohui Tang, Guo-Yuan Yang, Zhijun Zhang
pmc-10529757.description: Optogenetics has been used to regulate astrocyte activity and modulate neuronal function after brain injury. Activated astrocytes regulate blood-brain barrier functions and are thereby involved in brain repair. However, the effect and molecular mechanism of optogenetic-activated astrocytes on the change in barrier function in ischemic stroke remain obscure.

pmc-10736364.title: LONGEVITY DETERMINANTS IN AFRICAN AMERICANS: AN INTRA-GROUP ANALYSIS FROM THE HEALTH AND RETIREMENT STUDY
pmc-10736364.creator: Meneka Johnson Nicholson, Peter Martin
pmc-10736364.description: Utilizing the Health and Retirement Study data, this research exclusively centered on a sample of 2953 African-American participants to discern longevity predictors, emphasizing the importance of intra-group analysis. This targeted approach is essential as it provides a nuanced understanding of factors affecting longevity within a specific demographic group, avoiding broad generalizations derived from diverse populations.

pmc-11352194.title: The Role of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) in the Management of Metabolic Diseases in Humans: A Narrative Review
pmc-11352194.creator: Eva Zikou, Chrysi Koliaki, Konstantinos Makrilakis
pmc-11352194.description: The gut microbiota represents a complex ecosystem of trillions of microorganisms residing in the human gastrointestinal tract, which is known to interact with the host physiology and regulate multiple functions. Alterations in gut microbial composition, diversity, and function are referred to as dysbiosis.

pmc-11367507.title: The burden of allergic rhinitis is undermanaged in a large proportion of Chinese young adults from Singapore☆
pmc-11367507.creator: Qi Yi Ambrose Wong, Jun Jie Lim, Jun Yan Ng, Praneeth Malipeddi, Yi Ying Eliza Lim, Yang Yie Sio, Fook Tim Chew
pmc-11367507.description: BackgroundAllergic rhinitis (AR) is a nasal disorder characterized by the simultaneous manifestation of at least 2 out of 4 possible symptoms: rhinorrhea, nasal itching, nasal pruritus, and sneezing. Presently, among Chinese young adults from Singapore, we characterised AR phenotypes, established Total Nasal Symptom Score (TNSS) baselines, and examined the management of AR.

pmc-11398718.title: Association Between Eyelid Twitching and Digital Screen Time, Uncorrected Refractive Error, Intraocular Pressure, and Blood Electrolyte Imbalances
pmc-11398718.creator: Irfan B Gunes
pmc-11398718.description: Introduction: Previous studies have shown that isolated eyelid myokymia (EM) is usually caused by stress, fatigue, and caffeine consumption. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between EM and digital screen time, uncorrected refractive error, intraocular pressure (IOP), and blood electrolyte levels.

pmc-13207878.title: A Preoperative MRI-Based Score to Predict High-Risk Pathology and Stratify Adjuvant Therapy Benefit in BCLC 0/A Hepatocellular Carcinoma
pmc-13207878.creator: Huiying Li, Xinxin Wang, Can Yu, Baihe Li, Zhe Hu, Wanhu Li, Yueqin Chen, Yang Zhou, Yajuan Sun
pmc-13207878.description: PurposeThis study aims to develop and validate a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based preoperative scoring model for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) or Edmondson–Steiner grade 3/4 in BCLC 0/A hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and explore its potential for early recurrence risk stratification and as a hypothesis-generating tool for identifying patients who may benefit from adjuvant therapy.

pmc-13585253.title: Impact of traditional cooking methods on total phenolics, flavonoids, and antioxidant capacities of dark green leafy vegetables
pmc-13585253.creator: Bahar Yalçın Çeliktaş, Muazzez Garipağaoğlu, Şeyda Karaman Ersoy
pmc-13585253.description: This study evaluated the effects of four domestic cooking methods—steaming, microwaving, low-water boiling and high-water boiling—on the phenolic composition and antioxidant capacities of five dark green leafy vegetables (sorrel, stinging nettle, spinach, Swiss chard and purslane). Total phenolics, phenolic acids, flavonoids and tannins were quantified spectrophotometrically, while antioxidant capacities were assessed by DPPH, ABTS and CUPRAC assays.

uslaw-usc-t18-s1622.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1622 — Subornation of perjury
uslaw-usc-t18-s1622.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s1622.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 79 (Perjury). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever procures another to commit any perjury is guilty of subornation of perjury, and shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than five years, or both.
